subject: Life Skills
title: Framing Effects
description: A micro-lesson that makes Framing Effects usable.

hook.text: '90% fat-free' and '10% fat' describe the same yogurt. The first sells dramatically better. Same fact, different frame.

buildup.text: Kahneman and Tversky proved that how information is framed changes decisions more than the information itself.

discovery.text: Framing Effects reveals the mechanism or argument that changes the picture.

twist.text: Framing Effects has a twist: the obvious interpretation usually breaks down.

climax.text: Counter framing by restating the fact both ways. If someone says '90% success rate,' ask: 'What does the 10% look like?'

punchline.text: Same fact, opposite feel. Always flip the frame.

quiz.question: Why is loss framing more powerful than gain framing?
options: Losses are always larger than gains
People feel losses more intensely than equivalent gains
Loss framing is used more often in advertising
